Its whole value is one\nrule; internalize it before anything else:\n\n> **A claim is a FACT only when a deterministic oracle fires over data a real target\n> produced.** You (the LLM) ADVISE where to look and what a result might mean; the oracle\n> CONFIRMS. Nothing else — not your confidence, not a critic's endorsement, not a plausible\n> story — promotes a claim to a fact.\n\nThe standing doctrine every reasoning call operates under is\n[framework/cognitive/metacognition.md](../../../framework/cognitive/metacognition.md) (it is\ninjected into every LLM system prompt). The full architecture — agents, event spine, veracity\nlayer, learning/metacognition core, safety stack — is\n[framework/v2/docs/CRUCIBLE-AI.md](../../../framework/v2/docs/CRUCIBLE-AI.md). The binding\nconstitution is [CLAUDE.md](../../../CLAUDE.md); never relax scope, destruction, evidence, or\nhonesty rules.\n\n## The invariants (never violate these)\n\n1. **Oracle authority.** Only a fired oracle confirms. Critics/RL/reflection/self-consistency\n   may only *advise, re-rank, defer, or abstain* — never promote a finding or override the oracle.\n2. **Coverage.** Never silently skip an authorized attack surface. Learning and reflection\n   *deprioritise* (re-rank / defer); they never gate a surface out.\n3. **Prove by re-execution.** A finding is a fact only if its retained `oracle_context`\n   re-fires. The veracity firewall (`framework/v2/veracity/`) re-runs proofs; it can only demote.\n4. **Non-circular learning.** An EXPLOITABLE label needs ≥2 independent corroborating oracle\n   kinds; a silent oracle is never auto-labelled a false positive.\n5. **Refuse honestly, fail closed.** Decline to conclude what you cannot ground; record every\n   refusal as evidence. Hard limits (scope, authorization, destruction, real user data) are\n   inviolable — when unsure, stop and ask.\n6. **Determinism + append-only.** No wallclock/global-rng in learning/reward math; the event\n   spine is append-only (supersede, never edit).\n\n## Structured workflows\n\n### Run an authorized engagement (end-to-end, gated)\n1. Confirm the active target's `targets/<slug>/charter.md` authorizes it (constitution §II).\n2. `python3 -m framework.v2 engage <slug> <seed-url> [--recon] [--spine]`\n   — crawls, audits, confirms via oracles, chains attack paths, scores confidence, and\n   (with `--spine`) mirrors the whole run onto the immutable blackboard event stream.\n   (`--strict-evidence` is a **`scan`**-only flag, below — not an `engage` flag.)\n3. Every request passes the full gate chain; an out-of-scope seed or tripped kill-switch\n   refuses *before* traffic and is recorded as a `refusal` event.\n\n### Loopback-only quick scan\n`python3 -m framework.v2 scan http://127.0.0.1:<port>/ --format json|sarif|html [--strict-evidence]`\n— the export states each finding's **live grounding** (fact / ungrounded / contradicted);\n`--strict-evidence` withholds non-fact findings from the rendered doc but keeps them in\n`--reverifiable-out`.\n\n### Re-verify a report (prove-don't-guess, offline)\n`python3 -m framework.v2 verify <report.json>` re-runs each finding's retained `oracle_context`.\n`python3 -m framework.v2 evidence ...` builds/verifies signed, hash-linked evidence certificates\n(and, with report claims bound in, fails closed when a report sentence has no backing evidence).\n\n### Inspect / audit the event spine\nThe blackboard (`framework/v2/agents/blackboard.py`) is the one append-only, typed, provenance-\nlinked event stream. Replay it with `Blackboard.replay(engagement=..., since_id=...)`.\nCryptographic tamper-evidence: `framework/v2/agents/spine_chain.py`\n(`build_spine_chain` / `sign_spine_head` / `verify_spine_head`).\n\n### Recon / intel, memory, self-improvement\n`python3 -m framework.v2 intel ...` (OSINT into the shared world-model; gated egress),\n`memory ...` (cross-engagement priors — never fabricate a score), `improve ...`\n(authorise-not-apply — it never self-applies a change).\n\n### Read-only operator console\n`python3 -m framework.v2 console` — loopback, read-only, zero-impact operator UI over the run.\n\n## What NOT to do\n- Do not build detection-evasion / identity-rotation / stay-hidden-from-defenders capability —\n  CRUCIBLE is correlatable and authorized by doctrine (constitution §VI).\n- Do not let any learned/critic/LLM signal enter the deterministic oracle/SCE/calibration inputs\n  or promote a finding.\n- Do not attack third parties (payment/IdP/CDN) — test only the operator's integration with them.\n"}]},"isMeta":true,"uuid":"3b0ad2e1-01f5-4701-8cdb-6d21e4dac06e","timestamp":"2026-07-19T06:05:52.485Z","userType":"external","entrypoint":"claude-vscode","cwd":"/home/kali/Pictures/PENTEST-main","sessionId":"7758e121-f349-47d5-886b-6bb5a1d60e27","version":"2.1.214","gitBranch":"main","slug":"parsed-popping-lemur"}

Its records form the per-device nonce highwater.\n34\tRECEIPT_SIGNAL = \"mesh.request\"\n35\t\n36\t\n37\tdef envelope_message(core: dict) -> bytes:\n38\t    \"\"\"The exact bytes signed/verified — canonical JSON of the core. Returns (True, core) or (False, reason).\"\"\"\n60\t    p = payload.payload if hasattr(payload, \"payload\") else payload\n61\t    sig = p.get(\"sig\")\n62\t    device = p.get(\"device\")\n63\t    if not sig or not device:\n64\t        return False, \"missing signature or device\"\n65\t    if device not in authorized:                       # trust pinned to owner-minted device keys\n66\t        return False, \"device is not authorized\"\n67\t    core = {k: v for k, v in p.items() if k != \"sig\"}\n68\t    try:                                               # verify_one RAISES on a malformed-length sig\n69\t        sig_ok = verify_one(device, envelope_message(core), sig)\n70\t    except Exception:  # noqa: BLE001 — any crypto/decode error is a fail-closed refusal, never a crash\n71\t        return False, \"signature invalid\"\n72\t    if not sig_ok:\n73\t        return False, \"signature invalid\"\n74\t    if core.get(\"action\") not in ACTIONS:              # allow-list the authenticated action (fail-closed)\n75\t        return False, f\"unknown action: {core.get('action')!r}\"\n76\t    return True, core\n77\t\n78\t\n79\tdef record_receipt(store: SpineStore, core: dict) -> int:\n80\t    \"\"\"Append the append-only consumption receipt. It binds a `bind_ok` address (loopback or a PRIVATE/WireGuard address) — NEVER\n8\t    0.0.0.0 / a public address. The constructor asserts this; the CLI asserts it too. This is the\n9\t    non-negotiable exposure guard: the tunnel, not the transport, is the network boundary.\n10\t\n11\t  • THE AUTH. There is NO wire bearer secret (the ui's printed token is gone). Authentication IS a\n12\t    per-request Ed25519 signature the phone makes with ITS OWN owner-authorized device key — the\n13\t    Wave-1 device envelope (`bridge.envelope`). Binding the\n57\t# authenticated action to the endpoint stops a captured lesser-scoped envelope (e.g. `read:pending`,\n58\t# which leaks only {seq,tier,kind}) from being replayed against a more-sensitive endpoint (e.g.\n59\t# `read:recall`, which surfaces the owner's on-screen OCR history). `/api/graph` piggybacks on the\n60\t# `read:snapshot` scope: graph returns only aggregate health, strictly LESS sensitive than the\n61\t# snapshot, so a snapshot-scoped envelope reaching it is not an escalation (and a lesser envelope\n62\t# still cannot reach it).\n63\t_READ_ACTION = {\n64\t    \"/api/pending\": \"read:pending\",\n65\t    \"/api/snapshot\": \"read:snapshot\",\n66\t    \"/api/graph\": \"read:snapshot\",\n67\t    \"/api/stream\": \"read:stream\",\n68\t    \"/api/recall\": \"read:recall\",\n69\t}\n70\t\n71\t\n72\tclass BridgeServer(ThreadingHTTPServer):\n73\t    daemon_threads = True\n74\t\n75\t    def __init__(self, addr, handler, *, spine_path, trusted_pubkey=None, clock=None,\n76\t                 ts_window: float = _TS_WINDOW):\n77\t        host = addr[0]\n78\t        if not bind_ok(host):\n79\t            raise ValueError(\n80\t                f\"refusing to bind {host!r}: the bridge binds loopback or a PRIVATE (WireGuard) \"\n81\t                f\"address only — never 0.0.0.0 / an unspecified / a public address\")\n82\t        super().__init__(addr, handler)\n83\t        self.spine_path = Path(spine_path)\n84\t        # the owner PUBLIC key is the trust anchor (injectable for tests); NO private key ever lives here\n85\t        self.trusted_pubkey = trusted_pubkey if trusted_pubkey is not None else owner_pubkey()\n86\t        self.clock = clock or time.time          # injectable wallclock so the freshness gate is deterministic\n87\t        self.ts_window = ts_window\n88\t        port = self.server_address[1]            # the ACTUAL bound port (correct even for port 0)\n89\t        hosts = {f\"{host}:{port}\"}\n90\t        origins = {f\"http://{host}:{port}\"}\n91\t        if ipaddress.ip_address(host).is_loopback:   # dev convenience only — not added for a WG bind\n92\t            hosts |= {f\"127.0.0.1:{port}\", f\"localhost:{port}\"}\n93\t            origins |= {f\"http://127.0.0.1:{port}\", f\"http://localhost:{port}\"}\n94\t        self.allowed_hosts = frozenset(hosts)\n95\t        self.allowed_origins = frozenset(origins)\n96\t\n97\t    def store(self) -> SpineStore:\n98\t        return SpineStore(self.spine_path)       # fresh read each request (cheap, current)\n99\t\n100\t    def daemon(self) -> BridgeDaemon:\n101\t        return BridgeDaemon(self.store(), trusted_pubkey=self.trusted_pubkey)\n102\t\n103\t\n104\tdef _json_bytes(obj) -> bytes:\n105\t    return json.dumps(obj, ensure_ascii=False).encode(\"utf-8\")\n106\t\n107\t\n108\tclass Handler(BaseHTTPRequestHandler):\n109\t    server_version = \"sigil-bridge/1.0\"\n110\t    timeout = 30                                  # per-connection socket timeout (no hung reader)\n111\t    _MAX_BODY = 65536                             # bodies are tiny; cap to avoid a Content-Length hang/alloc\n112\t\n113\t    # never log auth (an envelope can ride in ?env= for SSE; never write it to a log)\n114\t    def log_message(self, fmt, *args):  # noqa: A003\n115\t        pass\n116\t\n117\t    # --- request helpers --------------------------------------------------------------------------\n118\t    def _query(self) -> dict:\n119\t        return parse_qs(urlparse(self.path).query)\n120\t\n121\t    def _authorized_now(self):\n122\t        \"\"\"The owner-minted authorized-device set, recomputed PER REQUEST — a revoke takes effect now.\"\"\"\n123\t        return authorized_devices(self.server.store(), self.server.trusted_pubkey)\n124\t\n125\t    def _envelope_payload(self):\n126\t        \"\"\"The device envelope: base64url of canonical JSON, in `X-SIGIL-Envelope` (GET/POST) or the\n127\t        `?env=` query (SSE, which cannot set a header). Applied to the whole POST action\n201\t        plane as defense-in-depth.\"\"\"\n202\t        if self.headers.get(\"Host\", \"\") not in self.server.allowed_hosts:\n203\t            return False\n204\t        o = self.headers.get(\"Origin\") or \"\"\n205\t        ref = self.headers.get(\"Referer\") or \"\"\n206\t        if o and o not in self.server.allowed_origins:\n207\t            return False\n208\t        if ref and not any(ref.startswith(a + \"/\") or ref == a for a in self.server.allowed_origins):\n209\t            return False\n210\t        return True\n211\t\n212\t    # It\n2\treuses the owner-signed cores: the queue (`approvals.pending` with the authorized-device set), a\n3\tDEVICE-signed approval (accepted only while that device is authorized), a PANIC halt (any engage is\n4\tfail-safe), and a KERNEL command relay (`KernelDispatch` → the same WARDEN gate as voice/UI).\n5\t\n6\tThis module is the bridge LIBRARY CORE + API (the doctrine + crypto). The network TRANSPORT — an\n7\tHTTP server over WireGuard, reusing the WS-C two-plane server pattern bound to a `bind_ok` address —\n8\tis a documented NEXT slice, not shipped here. `bind_ok` is the bind predicate that transport MUST\n9\tuse: loopback or a PRIVATE (WireGuard) address only — NEVER 0.0.0.0 / a public address.\"\"\"\n10\tfrom __future__ import annotations\n11\t\n12\timport ipaddress\n13\tfrom typing import List, Optional\n14\t\n15\tfrom ..spine.store import SpineStore\n16\t\n17\t\n18\t_CGNAT4 = ipaddress.ip_network(\"100.64.0.0/10\")   # carrier-grade NAT — the range Tailscale assigns tailnet IPs\n19\t\n20\t\n21\tdef bind_ok(addr: str) -> bool:\n22\t    \"\"\"True iff `addr` is safe to bind: loopback, a PRIVATE (e.g. WireGuard) address, or the CGNAT range\n23\t    Tailscale uses — never 0.0.0.0 / a public / an unspecified address.\"\"\"\n24\t    try:\n25\t        ip = ipaddress.ip_address(addr)\n26\t    except ValueError:\n27\t        return False\n28\t    if ip.is_unspecified:                          # 0.0.0.0 / :: → refuse\n29\t        return False\n30\t    return ip.is_loopback or ip.is_private or (ip.version == 4 and ip in _CGNAT4)\n31\t\n32\t\n33\tclass BridgeDaemon:\n34\t    def __init__(self, store: Optional[SpineStore] = None, *, trusted_pubkey: Optional[str] = None):\n35\t        from ..governor.identity import owner_pubkey\n36\t        self.store = store or SpineStore()\n37\t        # the owner trust anchor — the persisted identity by default (injectable for tests)\n38\t        self.trusted_pubkey = trusted_pubkey if trusted_pubkey is not None else owner_pubkey()\n39\t\n40\t    def _authorized(self):\n41\t        from ..mesh import authorized_devices\n42\t        return authorized_devices(self.store, self.trusted_pubkey)\n43\t\n44\t    def pending(self) -> List[dict]:\n45\t        \"\"\"The phone-facing queue — minimal fields only (no subject leaks over the tunnel).\"\"\"\n46\t        from ..agents.approvals import pending\n47\t        items = pending(self.store, self.trusted_pubkey, extra_pubkeys=self._authorized())\n48\t        return [{\"seq\": r.seq, \"tier\": r.payload.get(\"tier\"), \"kind\": r.kind} for r in items]\n49\t\n50\t    def recall(self, subject: str) -> Optional[dict]:\n51\t        \"\"\"Read-only remote RECALL — \"where did I last see X?\" — answered from the owner's own\n52\t        GROUNDED on-screen OCR history. Returns the perception-recall provenance dict VERBATIM\n53\t        (seq/entry_hash/when/frame_sha256/quote) or None: A0, read-only, no VLM and no paraphrase —\n54\t        the served `quote` is the owner's verbatim captured OCR line, never an advisory VLM lead.\n55\t\n56\t        This surfaces the owner's own on-screen text over the tunnel, so it leaks MORE than\n57\t        `pending()`'s minimal {seq,tier,kind} fields. The network SERVER (a later slice) MUST\n58\t        therefore gate this behind an authorized-device (device-signed) read request; this daemon\n59\t        method is only the read-only core.\"\"\"\n60\t        from ..perception.recall import recall\n61\t        return recall(self.store, subject)\n62\t\n63\t    def submit_device_approval(self, payload: dict) -> int:\n64\t        \"\"\"Append a DEVICE-signed approval the phone produced — ONLY if the signing device is\n65\t        currently authorized AND the signature verifies (fail-closed). A rogue/revoked device or a\n66\t        forged signature is refused; the signed target_seq binds (no replay).\"\"\"\n67\t        from ..agents.approvals import SIGNAL as APPROVAL_SIGNAL\n68\t        from ..agents.approvals import verify_approval\n69\t\n70\t        class _Rec:\n71\t            def __init__(self, p): self.payload = p\n72\t        authorized = self._authorized()\n73\t        if payload.get(\"signal\") != APPROVAL_SIGNAL:\n74\t            raise ValueError(\"not an approval record\")\n75\t        if payload.get(\"pubkey\") not in authorized:\n76\t            raise ValueError(\"signing device is not authorized\")\n77\t        if not verify_approval(_Rec(payload), self.trusted_pubkey, extra_pubkeys=authorized):\n78\t            raise ValueError(\"approval signature invalid\")\n79\t        sig, tgt = payload.get(\"sig\"), payload.get(\"target_seq\")\n80\t        # Best-effort dedup OUTSIDE the append lock (a rare concurrent double-record is benign; holding the\n81\t        # lock across an O(spine) scan would stall every other writer). The live\n93\t        SessionGate RE-VERIFIES and enforces freshness / kill-switch / single-session / TTL when it\n94\t        consumes this via `arm_by_device`, so recording is necessary-but-not-sufficient to arm.\"\"\"\n95\t        from ..gesture.session import ARM_REQUEST, _ARM_CORE, arm_request_message\n96\t        from ..reuse import verify_one\n97\t        authorized = self._authorized()\n98\t        if request.get(\"signal\") != ARM_REQUEST:\n99\t            raise ValueError(\"not an arm request\")\n100\t        pub = request.get(\"pubkey\")\n101\t        if pub not in authorized:\n102\t            raise ValueError(\"signing device is not authorized\")\n103\t        core = {k: request.get(k) for k in _ARM_CORE}\n104\t        try:                                            # verify_one RAISES on a malformed-length sig — refuse cleanly\n105\t            ok = verify_one(pub, arm_request_message(core), request.get(\"sig\", \"\"))\n106\t        except Exception:  # noqa: BLE001\n107\t            ok = False\n108\t        if not ok:\n109\t            raise ValueError(\"arm request signature invalid\")\n110\t        sig = request.get(\"sig\")\n111\t        # already recorded — idempotent, no spine bloat\n116\t        # record ONLY the signed core + pubkey + sig (never `**request` — no unsigned extras persisted)\n117\t        return self.store.append(kind=\"event\", source=\"mesh\", actor=\"DEVICE\",\n118\t                                 payload={\"signal\": ARM_REQUEST, \"device_id\": core[\"device_id\"],\n119\t                                          \"nonce\": core[\"nonce\"], \"ts\": core[\"ts\"],\n120\t                                          \"ttl_seconds\": core[\"ttl_seconds\"], \"pubkey\": pub, \"sig\": sig,\n121\t                                          \"tier\": \"A0\", \"decision\": \"auto\"})\n122\t\n123\t    def panic_engage(self, *, by: str = \"phone\") -> int:\n124\t        \"\"\"Halt the mesh from the phone. Two enforcement layers so a gesture can NEVER trigger an unintended action:\n3\t\n4\t  Layer 1 — the SESSION: `arm()` REQUIRES the owner key (it cannot be armed without the owner\n5\t  identity) and appends a signed `gesture.session_armed` record — the tamper-evident AUDIT proof-of-\n6\t  authorization, indicator-lit. A2 (type/combo/app.launch) is QUEUED for a\n12\t  verified owner/device approval bound to `sha256(session_id|tool|args)` and NEVER auto-injected — so\n13\t  a gesture alone can never type a password or launch an app.\n14\t\n15\tOnly arm/disarm + DISCRETE actions (click/scroll/drag injected; type/launch queued) hit the spine —\n16\tper-frame pointer MOVES are telemetry (30 FPS records would DoS the append-only log).\"\"\"\n17\tfrom __future__ import annotations\n18\t\n19\timport math\n20\timport time\n21\timport uuid\n22\tfrom dataclasses import dataclass\n23\tfrom typing import Optional\n24\t\n25\t_KS_CACHE_TTL = 0.5    # bound the per-intent kill-switch consult to ≤2 spine scans/sec (never per-frame at 30fps)\n26\t\n27\tfrom ..agents.base import Tier\n28\tfrom ..reuse import sha256_hex\n29\tfrom .components import InputBackend\n30\tfrom .types import GestureIntent\n31\t\n32\tSESSION_ARMED = \"gesture.session_armed\"\n33\tSESSION_DISARMED = \"gesture.session_disarmed\"\n34\tACTION_SIGNAL = \"gesture.action\"\n35\tARM_REQUEST = \"gesture.arm_request\"\n36\t\n37\tMAX_DEVICE_TTL = 300.0        # a DEVICE-armed session is deliberately SHORTER than a local owner arm (1800)\n38\tARM_FRESHNESS = 30.0          # a device arm request must be recent (anti-stale / bounds the replay window)\n39\t_ARM_CORE = (\"signal\", \"device_id\", \"nonce\", \"ts\", \"ttl_seconds\")\n40\t\n41\tINTENT_TOOL = {\n42\t    \"move\": \"hid.pointer.move\", \"click\": \"hid.pointer.click\",\n43\t    \"scroll_left\": \"hid.pointer.scroll\", \"scroll_right\": \"hid.pointer.scroll\",\n44\t    \"drag\": \"hid.pointer.drag\", \"type\": \"hid.type\", \"combo\": \"hid.combo\", \"launch\": \"hid.app.launch\",\n45\t}\n46\t\n47\t\n48\tdef pending_device_arms(store, trusted_pubkey=None):\n49\t    \"\"\"ALL RECORDED device arm requests (written by the bridge's `submit_arm_request`) that have NOT yet\n50\t    armed a session, OLDEST-FIRST — candidates for `arm_by_device`, which RE-VERIFIES each fully (auth /\n51\t    freshness / kill-switch / replay / single-session / TTL). Returns a list (possibly empty). Oldest-first\n52\t    + returning ALL candidates means a newer STALE request never shadows an older still-valid one. This is\n53\t    the wiring that makes the remote-arm path reachable end-to-end (the gesture daemon consumes it).\"\"\"\n54\t    armed = set()\n55\t    cands = []\n56\t    for r in store.iter_records():\n57\t        p = r.payload\n58\t        if p.get(\"signal\") == SESSION_ARMED and p.get(\"armed_by\") == \"device\":\n59\t            armed.add((p.get(\"device_pubkey\"), p.get(\"nonce\")))\n60\t        elif (p.get(\"signal\") == ARM_REQUEST and p.get(\"decision\") == \"auto\"\n61\t              and p.get(\"sig\") and p.get(\"pubkey\")):\n62\t            cands.append(dict(p))\n63\t    return [c for c in cands if (c.get(\"pubkey\"), c.get(\"nonce\")) not in armed]\n64\t\n65\t\n66\tdef arm_request_message(core: dict) -> bytes:\n67\t    \"\"\"The canonical bytes a device signs to request an arm — ONLY the signed core fields, so a caller\n68\t    cannot smuggle unsigned extras. Mirrors the approval/envelope canonical-json contract.\"\"\"\n69\t    from ..reuse import canonical_json\n70\t    m = canonical_json({k: core.get(k) for k in _ARM_CORE})\n71\t    return m if isinstance(m, bytes) else m.encode(\"utf-8\")\n72\t\n73\t\n74\tdef sign_arm_request(device_key, *, device_id: str, nonce, ts: float, ttl_seconds: float) -> dict:\n75\t    \"\"\"Phone-side: build a device-signed arm request. The device signs with its OWN key (never the owner\n76\t    trust-root); the owner authorized this device once via the mesh ledger. This is the credential the\n77\t    bridge records and `SessionGate.arm_by_device` verifies.\"\"\"\n78\t    from ..reuse import sign\n79\t    core = {\"signal\": ARM_REQUEST, \"device_id\": device_id, \"nonce\": nonce, \"ts\": ts, \"ttl_seconds\": ttl_seconds}\n80\t    return {**core, \"pubkey\": device_key.public_key_b64,\n81\t            \"sig\": sign(device_key.private_key_b64, arm_request_message(core))}\n82\t\n83\t\n84\t@dataclass\n85\tclass Session:\n86\t    session_id: str\n87\t    live: bool = True\n88\t    expires_at: float = 0.0            # wallclock deadline — a session is BOUNDED, never indefinite\n89\t\n90\t    def expired(self, now: float) -> bool:\n91\t        return self.expires_at > 0.0 and now >= self.expires_at\n92\t\n93\t\n94\tclass SessionGate:\n95\t    def __init__(self, store, backend: InputBackend, *, classifier=None, owner_key=None, trusted_pubkey=None):\n96\t        self.store = store\n97\t        self.backend = backend\n98\t        self._classifier = classifier\n99\t        self._owner_key = owner_key\n100\t        self._trusted_pubkey = trusted_pubkey\n101\t        self.session: Optional[Session] = None\n102\t        self._ks_engaged = False\n103\t        self._ks_checked_at = -1e9        # forces a fresh check on the first consult\n104\t\n105\t    def _trusted(self):\n106\t        if self._trusted_pubkey is None:\n107\t            from ..governor.identity import owner_pubkey\n108\t            self._trusted_pubkey = owner_pubkey()\n109\t        return self._trusted_pubkey\n110\t\n111\t    def _killswitch_engaged(self, now: float) -> bool:\n112\t        \"\"\"Kill-switch state, cached for ≤_KS_CACHE_TTL so a 30fps `handle` loop does not re-scan the\n113\t        append-only spine per frame (that scan is O(spine) — a self-DoS). Panic latency is bounded by\n114\t        the TTL. The arm path checks the kill-switch FRESH (uncached), so arming can never race a halt.\"\"\"\n115\t        if now - self._ks_checked_at >= _KS_CACHE_TTL:\n116\t            from ..governor.killswitch import KillSwitch\n117\t            self._ks_engaged = KillSwitch(self.store).is_engaged()\n118\t            self._ks_checked_at = now\n119\t        return self._ks_engaged\n120\t\n121\t    def _cls(self):\n122\t        if self._classifier is None:\n123\t            from ..agents.kernel_classify import KernelClassifier\n124\t            self._classifier = KernelClassifier()\n125\t        return self._classifier\n126\t\n127\t    # --- Layer 1: the owner-armed session ---------------------------------------------------------\n128\t    def arm(self, *, owner_key=None, ttl_seconds: float = 1800.0) -> Session:\n129\t        from ..governor.authn import signed_payload\n130\t        from ..governor.identity import owner_keypair\n131\t        ok = owner_key if owner_key is not None else (self._owner_key or owner_keypair())\n132\t        if ok is None:\n133\t            raise RuntimeError(\"cannot arm a gesture session without the owner key (BLOCK-3)\")\n134\t        sid = uuid.uuid4().hex\n135\t        core = {\"signal\": SESSION_ARMED, \"session_id\": sid}\n136\t        self.store.append(kind=\"event\", source=\"gesture\", actor=\"OWNER\",\n137\t                          payload={**signed_payload(core, ok), \"tier\": \"A0\", \"decision\": \"auto\",\n138\t                                   \"ttl_seconds\": ttl_seconds,\n139\t                                   \"summary\": \"gesture session ARMED (indicator lit — opt-in)\"})\n140\t        self.session = Session(sid, live=True, expires_at=time.time() + ttl_seconds)\n141\t        return self.session\n142\t\n143\t    def disarm(self) -> None:\n144\t        if self.session is not None:\n145\t            self.store.append(kind=\"event\", source=\"gesture\", actor=\"OWNER\",\n146\t                              payload={\"signal\": SESSION_DISARMED, \"session_id\": self.session.session_id,\n147\t                                       \"tier\": \"A0\", \"decision\": \"auto\", \"summary\": \"gesture session DISARMED\"})\n148\t            self.session.live = False\n149\t        self.session = None\n150\t\n151\t    # --- Layer 1b: DEVICE-signed remote arm (a deliberate, reviewed trust-widening) ----------------\n152\t    def arm_by_device(self, request: dict, *, now: Optional[float] = None) -> Optional[Session]:\n153\t        \"\"\"Arm on a VERIFIED, owner-authorized DEVICE signature (SIGIL §remote-arm). Every downstream\n154\t        bound is UNCHANGED — the A1-inject/A2-queue tier gate, the TTL, hand-loss/expiry disarm, and an\n155\t        owner disarm/kill that always wins. Fail-closed at each step; a refusal is recorded, never armed.\"\"\"\n156\t        from ..governor.killswitch import KillSwitch\n157\t        from ..mesh import authorized_devices\n158\t        from ..reuse import verify_one\n159\t        now = time.time() if now is None else now\n160\t        # (1) kill-switch FIRST — an owner halt (incl. a phone panic) beats any arm.\n161\t        if KillSwitch(self.store).is_engaged():\n162\t            return self._refuse_arm(request, \"kill-switch engaged\")\n163\t        # (2) owner-minted device key + valid signature over the signed core (RP-APPROVAL-2: the\n164\t        #     authorized set is owner-signed only, so a merely-presented key is never trusted).\n165\t        if request.get(\"signal\") != ARM_REQUEST:\n166\t            return self._refuse_arm(request, \"not an arm request\")\n167\t        pub = request.get(\"pubkey\")\n168\t        authorized = authorized_devices(self.store, self._trusted())\n169\t        core = {k: request.get(k) for k in _ARM_CORE}\n170\t        try:                                            # verify_one RAISES on a malformed-length sig — treat as refusal\n171\t            sig_ok = bool(pub) and pub in authorized and verify_one(pub, arm_request_message(core), request.get(\"sig\", \"\"))\n172\t        except Exception:  # noqa: BLE001 — any crypto/decoding error is a fail-closed refusal, never a crash\n173\t            sig_ok = False\n174\t        if not sig_ok:\n175\t            return self._refuse_arm(request, \"unauthorized or invalid device signature\")\n176\t        # (3) freshness — bounds the replay window and rejects a stale captured request. Written\n177\t        #     fail-CLOSED for non-finite input: `nan > 30` is False, so a signed NaN ts would slip a\n178\t        #     `>`-style gate; require finite AND within-window explicitly.\n179\t        try:\n180\t            ts = float(request.get(\"ts\"))\n181\t        except (TypeError, ValueError):\n182\t            return self._refuse_arm(request, \"missing/invalid timestamp\")\n183\t        if not math.isfinite(ts) or not (abs(now - ts) <= ARM_FRESHNESS):\n184\t            return self._refuse_arm(request, \"stale or non-finite timestamp\")\n185\t        # (4) replay — this (device, nonce) must not have armed before (the append-only spine is witness).\n186\t        nonce = request.get(\"nonce\")\n187\t        for r in self.store.iter_records():\n188\t            p = r.payload\n189\t            if (p.get(\"signal\") == SESSION_ARMED and p.get(\"armed_by\") == \"device\"\n190\t                    and p.get(\"device_pubkey\") == pub and p.get(\"nonce\") == nonce):\n191\t                return self._refuse_arm(request, \"replayed arm nonce\")\n192\t        # (5) single live session — a device arm NEVER displaces an existing/owner session.\n193\t        if self.session is not None and self.session.live and not self.session.expired(now):\n194\t            return self._refuse_arm(request, \"a gesture session is already live\")\n195\t        # (6) TTL clamp — shorter than a local owner arm; a deliberate trust-narrowing inside the widening.\n196\t        #     Reject non-finite/non-positive BEFORE the min() (min(nan,300)=nan → a never-expiring session).\n197\t        try:\n198\t            raw_ttl = float(request.get(\"ttl_seconds\", MAX_DEVICE_TTL))\n199\t        except (TypeError, ValueError):\n200\t            return self._refuse_arm(request, \"invalid ttl\")\n201\t        if not math.isfinite(raw_ttl) or raw_ttl <= 0:\n202\t            return self._refuse_arm(request, \"non-finite or non-positive ttl\")\n203\t        ttl = min(raw_ttl, MAX_DEVICE_TTL)\n204\t        sid = uuid.uuid4().hex\n205\t        # The record's AUTHORIZATION is the verified device signature — self-verifying vs the owner-signed\n206\t        # device ledger; actor=DEVICE mirrors submit_device_approval. Store the ORIGINAL SIGNED core\n207\t        # fields (so the sig re-verifies for ANY ttl, incl. a clamped one) + the effective TTL separately,\n208\t        # and ONLY known fields (never `**request` — no unsigned extras persisted).\n209\t        self.store.append(kind=\"event\", source=\"gesture\", actor=\"DEVICE\",\n210\t                          payload={\"signal\": SESSION_ARMED, \"session_id\": sid, \"armed_by\": \"device\",\n211\t                                   \"device_id\": core[\"device_id\"], \"device_pubkey\": pub,\n212\t                                   \"nonce\": core[\"nonce\"], \"ts\": core[\"ts\"],\n213\t                                   \"ttl_seconds\": core[\"ttl_seconds\"],   # ORIGINAL signed value → sig re-verifies\n214\t                                   \"effective_ttl\": ttl,                 # the CLAMPED ttl actually enforced\n215\t                                   \"sig\": request.get(\"sig\"), \"pubkey\": pub, \"authorization\": \"device-signed\",\n216\t                                   \"tier\": \"A0\", \"decision\": \"auto\",\n217\t                                   \"summary\": \"gesture session ARMED by authorized device (remote)\"})\n218\t        self.session = Session(sid, live=True, expires_at=now + ttl)\n219\t        return self.session\n220\t\n221\t    def _refuse_arm(self, request: dict, reason: str) -> None:\n222\t        self.store.append(kind=\"refusal\", source=\"gesture\", actor=\"DEVICE\",\n223\t                          payload={\"signal\": ARM_REQUEST, \"decision\": \"refused\", \"tier\": \"A0\",\n224\t                                   \"device_id\": request.get(\"device_id\"), \"reason\": reason,\n225\t                                   \"summary\": f\"device gesture arm refused: {reason}\"})\n226\t        return None\n227\t\n228\t    # --- Layer 2: per-intent tier gate ------------------------------------------------------------\n229\t    def handle(self, intent: GestureIntent) -> dict:\n230\t        \"\"\"Authorize + act on ONE intent. Returns a verdict dict. Injection ONLY inside a live session\n231\t        and ONLY for A1 tools; A2+ queues for approval and injects NOTHING; a danger name → refused.\"\"\"\n232\t        if intent.kind == \"hand_lost\":\n233\t            self.disarm()\n234\t            return {\"injected\": False, \"reason\": \"hand lost — session disarmed\"}\n235\t        # An owner halt (incl. a phone panic_engage) neuters injection mid-session — critical for a\n236\t        # device-armed session the owner may not be watching. Cached (≤_KS_CACHE_TTL) so a 30fps loop\n237\t        # never re-scans the spine per frame; panic latency is bounded by the TTL.\n238\t        if self._killswitch_engaged(time.time()):\n239\t            self.disarm()\n240\t            return {\"injected\": False, \"reason\": \"kill-switch engaged — session disarmed\"}\n241\t        if self.session is None or not self.session.live:\n242\t            return {\"injected\": False, \"reason\": \"no armed session — injection refused\"}\n243\t        if self.session.expired(time.time()):             # BLOCK-2: a session is bounded, never indefinite\n244\t            self.disarm()\n245\t            return {\"injected\": False, \"reason\": \"session expired — disarmed\"}\n246\t        tool = INTENT_TOOL.get(intent.kind)\n247\t        if tool is None:\n248\t            return {\"injected\": False, \"reason\": f\"unknown intent {intent.kind}\"}\n249\t        tier = self._cls().classify(tool)                 # DERIVED, fail-closed A3 on any error\n250\t        args = f\"{intent.dx:.4f},{intent.dy:.4f},{intent.arg}\"\n251\t        if tier <= Tier.A1:\n252\t            self._inject(intent)\n253\t            # BLOCK-1: log the DISCRETE A1 injections that actually take effect (click/scroll/drag);\n254\t            # per-frame `move` is telemetry (logging it at 30 FPS would DoS the append-only spine).\n255\t            if intent.kind != \"move\":\n256\t                self.store.append(kind=\"event\", source=\"gesture\", actor=\"OWNER\",\n257\t                                  payload={\"signal\": ACTION_SIGNAL, \"decision\": \"auto\", \"tier\": tier.label(),\n258\t                                           \"tool\": tool, \"session_id\": self.session.session_id,\n259\t                                           \"summary\": f\"gesture {tool} injected\"})\n260\t            return {\"injected\": True, \"tier\": tier.label(), \"tool\": tool}\n261\t        # A2/A3 → QUEUE an approval bound to this exact action; inject NOTHING\n262\t        token = sha256_hex(f\"{self.session.session_id}|{tool}|{args}\".encode(\"utf-8\"))\n263\t        seq = self.store.append(kind=\"event\", source=\"gesture\", actor=\"PERCEPTION\",\n264\t                                payload={\"signal\": ACTION_SIGNAL, \"decision\": \"queued\",\n265\t                                         \"status\": \"awaiting-approval\", \"tier\": tier.label(),\n266\t                                         \"tool\": tool, \"action_token\": token, \"args\": args,\n267\t                                         \"subject\": f\"gesture action {tool} (awaiting approval)\"})\n268\t        return {\"injected\": False, \"queued\": seq, \"tier\": tier.label(), \"tool\": tool, \"action_token\": token}\n269\t\n270\t    def _inject(self, intent: GestureIntent) -> None:\n271\t        b = self.backend\n272\t        if intent.kind == \"move\" or intent.kind == \"drag\":\n273\t            b.move(intent.dx, intent.dy)\n274\t        elif intent.kind == \"click\":\n275\t            b.click()\n276\t        elif intent.kind == \"scroll_left\":\n277\t            b.scroll(-1, 0)\n278\t        elif intent.kind == \"scroll_right\":\n279\t            b.scroll(1, 0)\n280\t"}]},"uuid":"6b7f0b0c-f431-48b7-82a2-e0d5d76f8ffd","timestamp":"2026-07-19T06:06:27.530Z","sourceToolAssistantUUID":"74cb52ac-8c18-4360-8e6a-395ff9371b7a","userType":"external","entrypoint":"claude-vscode","cwd":"/home/kali/Pictures/PENTEST-main","sessionId":"7758e121-f349-47d5-886b-6bb5a1d60e27","version":"2.1.214","gitBranch":"main","slug":"parsed-popping-lemur"}

Graceful fallbacks; components are injectable so the\n4\twhole loop runs deterministically on scripted doubles with no camera/model/OS input.\"\"\"\n5\tfrom __future__ import annotations\n6\t\n7\tfrom typing import Optional\n8\t\n9\tfrom .pipeline import GesturePipeline\n10\tfrom .session import SessionGate\n11\t\n12\t\n13\tdef run_gesture(*, store=None, owner_key=None, source=None, landmarker=None, classifier=None,\n14\t                backend=None, pipeline=None, gate=None, max_frames: Optional[int] = None,\n15\t                auto_arm: bool = True, device_arm: bool = False, trusted_pubkey=None) -> int:\n16\t    \"\"\"Run the loop; returns the number of frames processed. Injectable for tests.\n17\t\n18\t    `auto_arm=True` (default) is the camera path: owner-arm the session locally on start. `auto_arm=False`\n19\t    is for a caller that passes an ALREADY-ARMED `gate` — e.g. a LOCAL owner-armed session consuming a\n20\t    `remote.RemoteLandmarkSource` (owner arms at the PC; the phone streams landmarks in).\n21\t\n22\t    `device_arm=True` (with `auto_arm=False`) is the REMOTE-arm path: while no session is live, each frame\n23\t    the loop consumes the newest RECORDED, not-yet-used device arm request (written by the bridge's\n24\t    `submit_arm_request`) via `SessionGate.arm_by_device`, which RE-VERIFIES it fully. Once armed, the\n25\t    phone's landmark stream drives the pointer, bounded exactly as a local arm (A1 inject / A2 queue,\n26\t    kill-switch/expiry/hand-loss disarm). This is the wiring that makes the trust-widening reachable.\"\"\"\n27\t    if store is None:\n28\t        from ..spine.store import SpineStore\n29\t        store = SpineStore()\n30\t    if source is None:\n31\t        from ..perception.camera_stream import CameraStreamSource\n32\t        source = CameraStreamSource()\n33\t    if landmarker is None:\n34\t        from .landmark import OnnxHandLandmarker\n35\t        landmarker = OnnxHandLandmarker()\n36\t    # STRICT fail-closed egress gate (Phase 9 W2-H): this loop injects HID off a live camera stream,\n37\t    # so it refuses UNLESS the landmarker is EXPLICITLY on-box (`egresses is False`) — stricter than\n38\t    # perceive's default-safe `getattr(..., \"egresses\", False)` form, because an unset/unknown flag\n39\t    # here would mean streaming owner PIXELS off-box while driving the pointer. This gate refuses a\n40\t    # model that would EGRESS owner imagery; a future `RemoteLandmarker` with `egresses=False` (an\n41\t    # authorized INBOUND landmark-DATA stream over the owner's own tunnel) is a DISTINCT,\n42\t    # separately-authorized thing — it egresses nothing and passes this gate.\n43\t    if getattr(landmarker, \"egresses\", True) is not False:\n44\t        store.append(kind=\"refusal\", source=\"gesture\", actor=\"OWNER\",\n45\t                     payload={\"signal\": \"gesture.refused\", \"decision\": \"refused\", \"tier\": \"A0\",\n46\t                              \"reason\": \"landmark model would egress owner imagery — the gesture \"\n47\t                                        \"loop is on-box only\"})\n48\t        return 0  # inject NOTHING; never armed\n49\t    if classifier is None:\n50\t        from .features import RuleClassifier\n51\t        classifier = RuleClassifier()\n52\t    if backend is None:\n53\t        from ..platform import input_backend\n54\t        backend = input_backend()\n55\t    pipe = pipeline or GesturePipeline()\n56\t    g = gate or SessionGate(store, backend, owner_key=owner_key, trusted_pubkey=trusted_pubkey)\n57\t    if auto_arm:\n58\t        g.arm(owner_key=owner_key)   # camera path: owner-arm locally. When False, the caller's gate is\n59\t        # already armed (a LOCAL owner-armed session) and we consume it without a second arm.\n60\t    n = 0\n61\t    _attempted: set = set()\n62\t    try:\n63\t        for frame in source.frames():\n64\t            if device_arm and (g.session is None or not g.session.live):\n65\t                from .session import pending_device_arms    # REMOTE-arm: consume recorded arm requests\n66\t                for req in pending_device_arms(store, trusted_pubkey):   # oldest-first — a newer stale one\n67\t                    _key = (req.get(\"pubkey\"), req.get(\"nonce\"))         # can't shadow an older valid one\n68\t                    if _key in _attempted:                  # attempt each recorded request ONCE (no per-frame\n69\t                        continue                            # refusal spam from a stale/refused request)\n70\t                    _attempted.add(_key)\n71\t                    if g.arm_by_device(req) is not None:    # re-verifies fully; stop once one arms\n72\t                        break\n73\t            reading = classifier.classify(landmarker.detect(frame))\n74\t            intent = pipe.on_frame(reading)\n75\t            if intent is not None:\n76\t                g.handle(intent)\n77\t            n += 1\n78\t            if max_frames is not None and n >= max_frames:\n79\t                break\n80\t    finally:\n81\t        g.disarm()\n82\t    return n\n83\t"}]},"uuid":"244cd193-e064-4c40-8f46-d1b6e1eccff5","timestamp":"2026-07-19T06:06:27.831Z","sourceToolAssistantUUID":"d05f7c26-0e52-4aa9-8379-3dcbba812c94","userType":"external","entrypoint":"claude-vscode","cwd":"/home/kali/Pictures/PENTEST-main","sessionId":"7758e121-f349-47d5-886b-6bb5a1d60e27","version":"2.1.214","gitBranch":"main","slug":"parsed-popping-lemur"}

The\n5\t`cert_digest` is over the record's CONTENT only (scope/kind/source/actor/payload/\n6\tparent/supersedes) — NOT the wallclock `ts` — so the chain is replay-stable. Appends\n7\tare O(1): read the last line's entry, `append_entry`, write.\n8\t\"\"\"\n9\tfrom __future__ import annotations\n10\t\n11\timport json\n12\timport os\n13\timport threading\n14\tfrom pathlib import Path\n15\tfrom typing import Any, Iterator\n16\t\n17\tfrom ..config import SCOPE, SPINE_PATH\n18\tfrom ..reuse import ChainEntry, append_entry, build_chain, digest_payload, verify_chain\n19\tfrom .models import SpineRecord, now_iso\n20\t\n21\ttry:\n22\t    import fcntl  # POSIX advisory file lock — cross-PROCESS append serialization\n23\texcept ImportError:  # pragma: no cover — non-POSIX\n24\t    fcntl = None  # type: ignore[assignment]\n25\t\n26\t_LOCKS_GUARD = threading.Lock()\n27\t_LOCKS: dict[str, \"threading.RLock\"] = {}\n28\t\n29\t\n30\tdef spine_lock(path: Path | str) -> \"threading.RLock\":\n31\t    \"\"\"A process-wide RE-ENTRANT lock per resolved spine path. Serializes `append` (read-tip → write)\n32\t    across threads so concurrent writers can't fork the hash chain, and — being re-entrant — lets a\n33\t    caller make a check-then-append atomic (e.g. the nonce replay gate) while its inner `append` still\n34\t    acquires the same lock. Cross-PROCESS serialization is added by an flock inside `append`.\"\"\"\n35\t    key = str(Path(path).resolve())\n36\t    with _LOCKS_GUARD:\n37\t        lk = _LOCKS.get(key)\n38\t        if lk is None:\n39\t            lk = _LOCKS[key] = threading.RLock()\n40\t        return lk\n41\t\n42\t\n43\tdef _last_nonempty_line(path: Path) -> str | None:\n44\t    \"\"\"Read the last non-empty line without loading the file (seek-from-end).\"\"\"\n45\t    with path.open(\"rb\") as f:\n46\t        f.seek(0, os.SEEK_END)\n47\t        end = f.tell()\n48\t        if end == 0:\n49\t            return None\n50\t        buf = b\"\"\n51\t        pos = end\n52\t        while pos > 0:\n53\t            step = min(8192, pos)\n54\t            pos -= step\n55\t            f.seek(pos)\n56\t            buf = f.read(step) + buf\n57\t            lines = [ln for ln in buf.split(b\"\\n\") if ln.strip()]\n58\t            if lines and (pos == 0 or buf.count(b\"\\n\") >= 2):\n59\t                return lines[-1].decode(\"utf-8\")\n60\t        lines = [ln for ln in buf.split(b\"\\n\") if ln.strip()]\n61\t        return lines[-1].decode(\"utf-8\") if lines else None\n62\t\n63\t\n64\tclass SpineStore:\n65\t    def __init__(self, path: Path | str = SPINE_PATH) -> None:\n66\t        self.path = Path(path)\n67\t        self.path.parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)\n68\t        self._last: ChainEntry | None = self._read_last_entry()\n69\t\n70\t    # --- write --------------------------------------------------------------------\n71\t    def append(\n72\t        self, *, kind: str, source: str, actor: str, payload: dict[str, Any],\n73\t        parent_id: int | None = None, supersedes_id: int | None = None,\n74\t        ts: str | None = None,\n75\t    ) -> int:\n76\t        content = {\n77\t            \"scope\": SCOPE, \"kind\": kind, \"source\": source, \"actor\": actor,\n78\t            \"payload\": payload, \"parent_id\": parent_id, \"supersedes_id\": supersedes_id,\n79\t        }\n80\t        cert_digest = digest_payload(content)  # wallclock-free\n81\t        # Serialize the whole read-tip → write so concurrent writers (threaded bridge server, gesture\n82\t        # daemon) can't both fork off a stale tip and break the chain. Re-read the TRUE tip from disk\n83\t        # under the lock — `self._last` may be stale if another instance/process appended.\n84\t        with spine_lock(self.path):\n85\t            with self.path.open(\"a\", encoding=\"utf-8\") as f:\n86\t                if fcntl is not None:\n87\t                    try:\n88\t                        fcntl.flock(f.fileno(), fcntl.LOCK_EX)   # cross-process guard (advisory)\n89\t                    except OSError:  # pragma: no cover\n90\t                        pass\n91\t                last = self._read_last_entry()\n92\t                entry = append_entry([last], cert_digest) if last else build_chain([cert_digest])[0]\n93\t                record = {\n94\t                    \"seq\": entry.seq, **content, \"ts\": ts or now_iso(),\n95\t                    \"cert_digest\": cert_digest, \"prev_hash\": entry.prev_hash, \"entry_hash\": entry.entry_hash,\n96\t                }\n97\t                f.write(json.dumps(record, ensure_ascii=False) + \"\\n\")\n98\t                f.flush()\n99\t            self._last = entry\n100\t        return entry.seq\n101\t\n102\t    # --- read ---------------------------------------------------------------------\n103\t    def iter_records(self, *, since_seq: int = -1) -> Iterator[SpineRecord]:\n104\t        if not self.path.exists():\n105\t            return\n106\t        with self.path.open(encoding=\"utf-8\") as f:\n107\t            for line in f:\n108\t                line = line.strip()\n109\t                if not line:\n110\t                    continue\n111\t                d = json.loads(line)\n112\t                if d[\"seq\"] > since_seq:\n113\t                    yield SpineRecord.from_dict(d)\n114\t\n115\t    def get(self, seq: int) -> SpineRecord | None:\n116\t        for r in self.iter_records(since_seq=seq - 1):\n117\t            if r.seq == seq:\n118\t                return r\n119\t            if r.seq > seq:\n120\t                break\n121\t        return None\n122\t\n123\t    @property\n124\t    def next_seq(self) -> int:\n125\t        return (self._last.seq + 1) if self._last else 0\n126\t\n127\t    def count(self) -> int:\n128\t        return sum(1 for _ in self.iter_records())\n129\t\n130\t    # --- integrity ----------------------------------------------------------------\n131\t    def entries(self) -> list[ChainEntry]:\n132\t        return [\n133\t            ChainEntry(seq=r.seq, prev_hash=r.prev_hash, cert_digest=r.cert_digest, entry_hash=r.entry_hash)\n134\t            for r in self.iter_records()\n135\t        ]\n136\t\n137\t    def verify(self) -> tuple[bool, str]:\n138\t        \"\"\"Two-layer UNKEYED integrity: (1) BINDING — each record's payload still hashes to its\n139\t        stored cert_digest (catches silent payload edits); (2) CHAIN — the entries link cleanly\n140\t        (catches delete/reorder/entry tamper). This proves internal CONSISTENCY, not authenticity:\n141\t        a naive payload edit fails (1), and a mid-chain digest edit cascades an entry_hash/prev_hash\n142\t        break caught by (2) — BUT a writer who recomputes cert_digest+entry_hash for the tip (no\n143\t        successor to cascade into) or forward-cascades a fork produces a self-consistent chain that\n144\t        passes here. Resistance to a recompute-capable writer is the owner-SIGNED head's job\n145\t        (`checkpoint.verify_checkpoint`, Ed25519 + monotonic last_seq).
